title: Pointwise cohomological bounds reconstruct a complex from truncations
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology] and let $E$ be an object of the derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ of the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose that for every point $x\in X$ there are a function $p_x:\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Z$ and a family $\mathfrak U_x$ of open neighborhoods of $x$ such that every open neighborhood of $x$ contains some member of $\mathfrak U_x$ (a fundamental system), and such that $H^p(U,H^{m-p}(E))=0$ for every $U\in\mathfrak U_x$ and every $p>p_x(m)$, with cohomology interpreted as in [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. For $n\geq0$ let $\tau_{\geq-n}E$ be the standard truncation [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], with its canonical map $c_n:E\to\tau_{\geq-n}E$; these form an inverse system with the canonical transition maps, and $c_n$ is compatible with them. Let $(K,p,\delta)$ be a derived limit of this system in $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-derived-limit] (the product $\prod_n\tau_{\geq-n}E$ being taken in $D(\mathcal O_X)$). Then there exists a morphism $c:E\to K$ with $\mathrm{pr}_n\circ p\circ c=c_n$ for all $n$, and every such morphism $c$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_X)$.

source.place: Tag 0D62, label lemma-is-limit-per-point, with Derived Categories Remark Tag 0H72 (remark-map-into-derived-limit-truncations: existence of c and independence of the choice)

proof.text: Put $K_n=\tau_{\geq-n}E$ and let $(K,p,\delta)$ be the chosen derived limit. The canonical maps $c_n:E\to K_n$ are compatible with the transitions $f_n:K_{n+1}\to K_n$, i.e. $c_n=f_n\circ c_{n+1}$; let $a:E\to\prod_nK_n$ be the morphism with $\mathrm{pr}_n\circ a=c_n$ [def-weil-derived-limit]. Then $\mathrm{pr}_n\circ(1-s)\circ a=c_n-f_n\circ c_{n+1}=0$ for every $n$, so $(1-s)\circ a=0$, and exactness of $\mathrm{Hom}(E,K)\to\mathrm{Hom}(E,\prod_nK_n)\to\mathrm{Hom}(E,\prod_nK_n)$ on the Roos triangle [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] gives $c:E\to K$ with $p\circ c=a$, i.e. $\mathrm{pr}_n\circ p\circ c=c_n$ for every $n$ (this is Derived Categories Remark Tag 0H72). For a fixed integer $m$ and every $n\geq-m$, the truncation map induces an isomorphism $H^m(E)\to H^m(K_n)$ by the defining property of the standard truncation [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 0D62, proof, first paragraph; derived.tex Tag 0H72

proof.text: Fix $x$ and $m$, and set $n(x)=\max\{0,\ 1+\max\{-m,\ p(x,m-1)-m,\ -1+p(x,m)-m,\ -2+p(x,m+1)-m\}\}$ (Tag 0D62's bound, raised to $0$ so that $K_{n(x)}$ is a member of the system indexed by $n\geq0$). Then $n(x)\geq-m$ and $n(x)\geq0$. For every $n\geq n(x)$, the three integers $m+n$, $m+n+1$, and $m+n+2$ are respectively larger than $p(x,m-1)$, $p(x,m)$, and $p(x,m+1)$. Since the cohomology sheaf in the truncation triangle is $H^{-n-1}(E)$, the pointwise hypothesis therefore gives $H^{m+n+i}(U,H^{-n-1}(E))=0$ for $i=0,1,2$ and every $U\in\mathfrak U_x$.

source.place: Tag 0D62, proof, choice of n(x) and final vanishing

proof.text: The distinguished triangle $H^{-n-1}(E)[n+1]\to K_{n+1}\to K_n\to H^{-n-1}(E)[n+2]$ is the successive-truncation triangle [lem-pc-derived-lower-truncation-step-triangle]. Its long exact cohomology sequence, together with the three vanishings from the preceding step, shows that for $n\geq n(x)$ and $U\in\mathfrak U_x$ both transition maps $H^{m-1}(U,K_{n+1})\to H^{m-1}(U,K_n)$ and $H^m(U,K_{n+1})\to H^m(U,K_n)$ are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0D62, proof, truncation triangle and long exact sequence

proof.text: Write $A_n=H^{m-1}(U,K_n)$ with transitions $g_n:A_{n+1}\to A_n$, which are isomorphisms for $n\geq n(x)$ by the preceding step. By [lem-pc-derived-limit-roos-abelian-groups], $R^1\varprojlim_nA_n\cong\operatorname{coker}(1-s)$, and $1-s$ is surjective: given $(a_n)_n$, put $b_{n(x)}=0$, $b_{n+1}=g_n^{-1}(b_n-a_n)$ for $n\geq n(x)$ and $b_n=a_n+g_n(b_{n+1})$ for $n<n(x)$ (descending); then $b_n-g_n(b_{n+1})=a_n$ for all $n$. Hence $R^1\varprojlim_n H^{m-1}(U,K_n)=0$; and the composites of the isomorphisms in degree $m$ give injections (indeed isomorphisms) $H^m(U,K_n)\to H^m(U,K_{n(x)})$ for all $n\geq n(x)$. Applying [lem-pc-ringed-space-derived-limit-stalk-injective], whose short exact sequence input is [lem-pc-ringed-space-rgamma-derived-limit], gives that $H^m(K)_x\to H^m(K_{n(x)})_x$, the map induced by $\mathrm{pr}_{n(x)}\circ p$, is injective. For any morphism $c:E\to K$ with $\mathrm{pr}_n\circ p\circ c=c_n$ for all $n$, its composite $H^m(E)_x\to H^m(K)_x\to H^m(K_{n(x)})_x$ is $H^m(c_{n(x)})_x$, the truncation isomorphism from Step 1 (as $n(x)\geq-m$), hence $H^m(E)_x\to H^m(K)_x$ is surjective, and injective since the composite is; so it is an isomorphism. This holds for every $x$ and $m$, so $H^m(c)$ is an isomorphism of sheaves for every $m$ and every such $c$ is an isomorphism in the derived category.
